source: AASB 1053 Application of Tiers of Australian Accounting Standards (compiled May 2022), Appendix A
text: Public accountability – an entity has public accountability if: (a) its debt or equity instruments are traded in a public market or it is in the process of issuing such instruments for trading in a public market (a domestic or foreign stock exchange or an over-the-counter market, including local and regional markets); or (b) it holds assets in a fiduciary capacity for a broad group of outsiders as one of its primary businesses.

The following for-profit entities are deemed to have public accountability: (a) disclosing entities, even if their debt or equity instruments are not traded in a public market or are not in the process of being issued for trading in a public market; (b) co-operatives that issue debentures; (c) registered managed investment schemes; (d) superannuation plans regulated by the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) other than Small APRA Funds as defined by APRA Superannuation Circular No. III.E.1 Regulation of Small APRA Funds, December 2000; and (e) authorised deposit-taking institutions.

The following types of entities shall prepare general purpose financial statements that comply with Tier 1 reporting requirements: (a) for-profit private sector entities that have public accountability and are required by legislation to prepare financial statements that comply with either Australian Accounting Standards or accounting standards; and (b) the Australian Government and State, Territory and Local Governments.

source: AASB 2020-2 Amendments to Australian Accounting Standards – Removal of Special Purpose Financial Statements for Certain For-Profit Private Sector Entities (F2020L00271), Objective

topic: ARS 701.0 — definition covering FX/trading results in EFS
source: Reporting Standard ARS 701.0 ABS/RBA Definitions for the EFS Collection (July 2019)
text: Holding gains / losses on assets and liabilities — Refers to realised and unrealised gains / losses on assets and liabilities. Realised gains / losses on assets and liabilities refer to changes in the value of assets and liabilities as a result of closing or disposal of assets and liabilities. Unrealised gains / losses on assets and liabilities refer to changes in the value of assets and liabilities as a result of changes in the market value of those assets and liabilities.
